faq.title: Big questions. A place to start.

items.question: I'm a U.S. citizen living in Canada. Do I still need to file?
items.answer: U.S. citizens are generally subject to U.S. tax rules on worldwide income, even while living abroad. Whether a return is required depends on factors such as income, age and filing status. Foreign account reporting may also apply.

items.question: Will I pay tax twice on the same income?
items.answer: Foreign tax credits and treaty provisions may help address double taxation, subject to eligibility and limits. They do not automatically remove filing requirements or every instance of tax in both countries.

items.question: Can I work with LeadTax remotely?
items.answer: Yes. Use the remote filing link to begin, or contact us first to discuss your cross-border situation and the appropriate way to share documents.

items.question: What if I haven't filed U.S. returns for several years?
items.answer: Start with a review of your filing history, income and accounts. Correction options depend on your facts. Any available relief procedure has eligibility requirements and should be assessed before filing.

items.question: How much will cross-border tax preparation cost?
items.answer: The fee depends on the countries and years involved, income sources and required forms. Contact us for a scope review and quote before work begins.
